terms.definition: A context-dependent relational representation of a complete army list before board placement.
A narrowed set of competitive legal actions under a chosen value and risk model.
Spatial, topological, graph, and combinatorial structure of a concrete board state.
Finite sample space of dice outcomes with a probability measure and rule-defined transformations.
A context region where list capability falls below a defined threshold.
A hidden structural model recovered from sparse measurements and used to generate a larger geometry.
Intuitive label for context-indexed board trajectories generated from fixed list and mission parameters.
Directed graph linking values, events, state fields, and rule operators.
Low-dimensional observable produced by projection from a richer state or history.
Log-ratio coordinate sigma(a,b)=log(a/b) for positive paired values.
Sequence of maps from rules and values through dice, transitions, histories, and outcomes.
Assignment of a value role based on operator behavior with another value in context.
Boundary or support representation for reachable or probable VP outcomes.
Compact coordinates which permit reconstruction and remain distinguishable under a model.
Two-dimensional space of score pairs (VP_A, VP_B).
Observed or projected score-advantage coordinate, often VP_A minus VP_B.
A total space locally equivalent to a product of a base neighborhood and typical fiber.
Assignment of one space to each context point.
Map from a fine input domain into a smaller set of discrete output bins.
Ability to factor a function, measure, or optimization into simpler components.
Space decomposed into pieces with regular local structure.
